exposure: parental concern for the child at age 2 years
cohort: 1781 children born in Southeast Sweden between October 1, 1997 and October 31, 1999
finding: Early psychosocial environment and mode of delivery were associated with the development of childhood abdominal pain, with non-vaginal birth associated with a reduced likelihood of developing abdominal pain.
mod_finding: Non-vaginal birth was associated with a reduced slope of the growth curve for abdominal pain, meaning children born via non-vaginal delivery were less likely to develop abdominal pain over time.
